```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown

from rse_survey_report.book import BOOK_CATEGORIES, BOOK_DIR, load_book_data
from rse_survey_report.config import NORDICS
from rse_survey_report.plotting import (
    plot_agreement,
    plot_choice,
    plot_likert2,
)
from rse_survey_report.utils import get_data_path, load_data, preprocess_data

codebook, df, df_compare = load_book_data()

df_all = preprocess_data(
    load_data(get_data_path("2026_tf.csv", 2026)), excl_var="submitdate_0"
)
df_submitted = df_all[df_all["complete"]]

n_rows = len(df_all)
n_submitted = len(df_submitted)
n_countries = df_submitted["country"].nunique()
n_nordic = len(df)
n_chapters = len(list((BOOK_DIR / "chapters").glob("*.qmd")))

BLUE = "#2a78d6"
GREY = "#b8b8b8"
```

# Method: background

## A Quarto book as a complement to the dashboard

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Dashboard**

- https://rse-survey.soton.ac.uk/superset/dashboard/RSE_survey/
- interactive dashboard for international RSE survey data
- focus: explorative data analysis

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Quarto book**

- new initiative
- One chapter for each survey question
- A fixed view on the Nordic countries
- Comparisons by age group and by country
- Built from code: the same data gives the same book
:::
::::

## Structure of the book

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Responses<br>2026_tf.csv"] --> C["Codebook<br>question type, answers, order"]
  B["Question text<br>2026_all_cols.csv"] --> C
  C --> D["Chapters<br>make book"]
  D --> E["Website<br>_book/"]
```

- `{python} len(BOOK_CATEGORIES)` parts, one for each topic.
  `{python} n_chapters` chapters, one for each closed question.
- Each chapter has four sections:
  - **Nordics**: all Nordic respondents
  - **By age group**: below 35, 35-45, 45+
  - **Within Nordics**: one group for each Nordic country
  - **Between countries**: Nordics, Germany, Netherlands
- Free-text questions have no chapter.

## Questions

**Topics, in survey order**

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("\n".join(f"- {name}" for name in BOOK_CATEGORIES))
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Question types**

```{python}
#| output: asis
formats = {
    "choice": "One or more options",
    "bool": "True or false",
    "likert": "Share of time, 0% to 100%",
    "agreement": "Five levels, disagree to agree",
    "text": "Free text",
}
n_questions = codebook.drop_duplicates("id")["type"].value_counts()
print("| Type | Answer format | Questions |\n| :-- | :-- | --: |")
for kind, text in formats.items():
    print(f"| `{kind}` | {text} | {n_questions.get(kind, 0)} |")
```
:::
::::

## Respondents per country

`{python} n_rows` responses. `{python} n_submitted` are submitted, from
`{python} n_countries` countries. The analysis uses the submitted responses
only.

```{python}
top = df_submitted["country"].value_counts().head(15).sort_values()
fig = px.bar(
    x=top.values,
    y=top.index,
    orientation="h",
    color=[
        "Nordic" if country in NORDICS else "Other" for country in top.index
    ],
    color_discrete_map={"Nordic": BLUE, "Other": GREY},
    labels={"x": "Submitted responses", "y": "", "color": ""},
    height=480,
)
fig.update_layout(plot_bgcolor="white")
fig.show()
```

## Focus on the Nordics

`{python} n_nordic` submitted responses from Finland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark,
Iceland and Estonia.

```{python}
nordic = df["country"].value_counts().reindex(NORDICS, fill_value=0)
fig = px.bar(
    x=nordic.index,
    y=nordic.values,
    text=nordic.values,
    color_discrete_sequence=[BLUE],
    labels={"x": "", "y": "Submitted responses"},
    height=420,
)
fig.update_layout(plot_bgcolor="white")
fig.show()
```

## Nordics: respondents per question

Respondents skip questions. Country-specific questions have few or no Nordic
responses.

```{python}
col_to_id = (
    codebook[codebook["col"].isin(df.columns)]
    .drop_duplicates("col")
    .set_index("col")["id"]
)
answered = df[col_to_id.index].notna().T.groupby(col_to_id, sort=False).any().T
answered = answered.loc[:, answered.any()]
per_question = answered.sum()
fig = px.bar(
    x=per_question.index,
    y=per_question.values,
    color_discrete_sequence=[BLUE],
    labels={"x": "Question id", "y": "Respondents"},
    height=480,
)
fig.update_layout(plot_bgcolor="white", xaxis_tickangle=-90, xaxis_dtick=1)
fig.update_xaxes(tickfont_size=8)
fig.show()
```
